communicationAssessment.issueBody:
## Problem

Little Say's tracked native release configuration has no Expo owner, project ID, or backend URL, so a clean checkout cannot resolve the existing release project. The user requested publishing-environment setup for Little Say and Calibrate on the ZBook.

## Requirements and acceptance

Record Little Say's verified existing Expo project (`@matthewchartier/little-say`) and the backend already documented in the README (`https://littlesay.darkmachines.net`). Keep signing credentials in local app data, outside Git.

- Change only the three nonsecret values in `native-release.json`; preserve app IDs, versions, channels, and release workflows.
- Show that the native release contract accepts the configuration and read-only EAS project inspection resolves the existing project.
- Run setup and release checks; distinguish these from an actual signed build, upload, or device test, which are outside this task.

This narrow setup outcome is separate from TestFlight preparation #12, optional grants #18/#20, and accounts #19/#24. It does not implement those features or establish iOS readiness. Calibrate's existing project access and prerequisite checks were verified separately; no Calibrate repository change is needed.

## Implementation plan

Record only the three verified nonsecret release values, preserve app identity/versions/channels, and validate configuration plus read-only EAS project resolution. Signing material stays outside Git; no native build, upload or distribution is part of this issue.

[Exact original requirements, plan and history](https://github.com/MChartier/agentic-development-workflow/blob/be7f2a00cbf9ced12d4b1a7a52f28e455695d7e3/issue-template-migration/little-say-25-original.md).

## Implementing Codex task


Verified implementing Codex task ID: `01a10f69-db3f-7763-b183-f0588d867033`. A shareable task link is not available through the current tools.

## Implementing PR

Current: [PR26: existing Expo project configuration](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/26). Source-review evidence and results remain in the PR.
communicationAssessment.prBody:
## Summary

Little Say's native release configuration leaves its Expo project and backend unset, so a clean checkout fails the release configuration check. This records the verified existing Expo project and the HTTPS backend already documented in the README, allowing the release tools to resolve the intended app.

Only three nonsecret values change. App IDs, versions, channels, and release workflows stay unchanged. Closes #25; independent of the TestFlight and accounts work.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

This is a non-UI configuration change. Against current master, the release contract rejects the unset owner; with these values it accepts the project and server origin. Read-only EAS inspection then resolves `@matthewchartier/little-say` with the exact configured project ID. [Observed results, source revisions, and reproduction commands](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/issues/25#issuecomment-6009578922).

## Supporting checks and limitations

Native setup and release metadata checks pass, as do all 18 existing release regression tests and diff hygiene. No signed native build, OTA publication, upload, deployment, or device test was performed. Signing credentials remain outside Git. [CI passes](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37415745229), including repository checks and PostgreSQL integration tests.
